name: Black dress of Rita Hayworth
subcategory: Iconic dress worn by Rita Hayworth in the film Gilda
summary: In the 1946 film Gilda, Rita Hayworth wore a black dress made by American costume designer Jean Louis.
description: In the 1946 film Gilda, Rita Hayworth wore a black dress made by American costume designer Jean Louis. It was used in a scene in which the character of Gilda sings the song "Put the Blame on Mame", improvising a quick striptease, choreographed by Jack Cole. The dress has helped consolidate the image of the femme fatale, as well as being universally recognized as an icon of fashion and cinema. The Independent named it as one of the Ten Best Fashion Moments in Film.
